decks.notes: The main focus of this deck is to quickly fill the graveyard with spells and then bring back Arclight Phoenix from the graveyard to deal fast, aggressive damage to the opponent. The deck utilizes cheap spells like Opt, Fiery Impulse, and Lightning Axe to trigger the ability of Arclight Phoenix and also includes card draw spells like Pieces of the Puzzle and Treasure Cruise to maintain card advantage. The inclusion of Thing in the Ice provides a backup win condition if Arclight Phoenix is not able to close out the game.

This deck focuses on using flying spirits to aggressively control the board and pressure the opponent's life total. By utilizing cards like Selfless Spirit and Spell Queller to protect key threats, while generating card advantage with cards like Supreme Phantom and Collected Company, the deck aims to maintain a fast tempo while disrupting the opponent's game plan. The mana base is carefully constructed to ensure consistent access to all colors needed for the deck's spell and creature requirements. With an emphasis on evasion and resilience, this deck seeks to overwhelm opponents quickly and efficiently.

The main focus of this Pioneer 1 vs 1 deck is to quickly ramp up mana using green devotion cards like Llanowar Elves and Elvish Mystic, while also utilizing powerful green creatures like Cavalier of Thorns and Old-Growth Troll to apply pressure and quickly overwhelm opponents. The deck also includes cards like Storm the Festival and Wolfwillow Haven to further accelerate mana production and card advantage. Additionally, the inclusion of planeswalkers like Nicol Bolas, Dragon-God and Teferi, Who Slows the Sunset provide additional utility and win conditions. Overall, the deck aims to establish a dominant board presence and outpace opponents in a competitive environment.

The main concept of this deck is to quickly ramp up mana using mana dorks like Llanowar Elves and Elvish Mystic, along with Nykthos, Shrine to Nyx, in order to play big threats like Old-Growth Troll and Cavalier of Thorns early in the game. The deck also utilizes green devotion to generate extra mana with cards like Wolfwillow Haven and Kiora, Behemoth Beckoner. Additionally, the deck includes powerful planeswalkers like Karn, the Great Creator and Teferi, Who Slows the Sunset to further disrupt the opponent and control the board.

This Esper Control deck focuses on maintaining board control and disrupting opponent's strategy through a combination of counterspells, removal spells, and card advantage. The main objective is to control the game tempo by using cards like Teferi, Hero of Dominaria and Shark Typhoon to generate value and outvalue the opponent. Additionally, the deck includes versatile removal options such as Supreme Verdict and Fatal Push to deal with threats efficiently. The mana base is designed to support the deck's color requirements while maximizing consistency and stability in casting spells.

The deck focuses on using Greasefang Parhelion alongside other creatures and spells to generate value and overwhelm the opponent. It combines graveyard synergies with card advantage and disruption to control the game while setting up for a powerful finish with the Parhelion II. The deck aims to quickly assemble its combo pieces and outvalue the opponent through efficient creature interactions and graveyard recursion. With a mix of aggressive threats and disruptive spells, it can adapt to various matchups and strategies, making it a versatile and potent combo deck in the Pioneer format.

The deck focuses on quickly assembling the combo of Greasefang and Parhelion II to generate a powerful board presence and overwhelm the opponent. It includes cards that help dig for combo pieces, disrupt the opponent's strategy, and protect the combo once assembled. The mana base is carefully constructed to support the deck's color requirements and maximize consistency. The goal is to efficiently execute the combo while controlling the game state and outvaluing the opponent.

The deck focuses on quickly filling the graveyard with spells and utilizing the Arclight Phoenix to continuously bring it back. It includes cards for card draw, removal, and protection to ensure the Phoenix can keep recurring. The main strategy is to cast multiple spells in a turn to trigger the Phoenix's ability to return from the graveyard, while also controlling the board with removal spells. It also includes alternative win conditions such as using Temporal Trespass and Treasure Cruise for card advantage and potentially overwhelming the opponent.

The deck focuses on utilizing the combination of Greasefang, Okiba Boss and Parhelion II to create a powerful board presence and overwhelm the opponent. It also runs a suite of disruption spells like Thoughtseize and Fatal Push to control the game and protect the combo pieces. The deck also includes cards like Bonecrusher Giant and Bloodtithe Harvester for additional value and removal options. Overall, the strategy of the deck is to assemble the combo pieces while disrupting the opponent's game plan to secure victory.

This deck focuses on using sacrifice effects to generate value and tempo, with cards like Mayhem Devil and Cauldron Familiar creating incremental advantages. It aims to disrupt the opponent's game plan by stealing their creatures with Claim the Firstborn and removing threats with Fatal Push. The deck also has a strong recursion element with cards like Kroxa, Titan of Death's Hunger and Fable of the Mirror-Breaker. Overall, the key strategy is to overwhelm the opponent with a constant stream of sacrificial plays and efficient removal, leading to a swift victory.

This Rakdos Sacrifice deck focuses on utilizing sacrifice mechanics to control the board and deal damage to the opponent. By sacrificing creatures with cards like Witch's Oven and Deadly Dispute, players can trigger effects from Mayhem Devil and Fable of the Mirror-Breaker to deal damage to the opponent. Claim the Firstborn and Eaten Alive also allow for stealing and sacrificing the opponent's creatures for additional value. The deck aims to overwhelm the opponent with a combination of aggressive creatures and removal spells, while maintaining a resource advantage through sacrificing and card draw effects.

The deck focuses on quickly establishing a board presence with Spirit creatures and utilizing tempo-based plays to control the game and keep the opponent on the back foot. By deploying evasive threats like Shacklegeist and Supreme Phantom, along with disruptive cards like Rattlechains and Geistlight Snare, the deck aims to apply pressure early on while maintaining a strong defensive position. Card draw and evasion are key components of the strategy, allowing the player to outmaneuver opponents and secure victory through efficient use of resources and combat tricks.

The main focus of this UW Control deck is to use counterspells, removal, and card advantage to control the game and outvalue the opponent. By utilizing cards like Teferi, Hero of Dominaria, Narset, Parter of Veils, and Search for Azcanta, the deck aims to generate card advantage and control the board. Cards like Supreme Verdict, Portable Hole, and Memory Deluge provide removal options for various threats, while Shark Typhoon and The Wandering Emperor offer a win condition. The mana base is designed to support the control game plan with utility lands and dual lands for consistency.
